topic: Open-Source Memory for Coding Agents, Synced Over SSH

key_points: Memory for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor + 17 others); indexes sessions agents already wrote to disk, including months before install, and recalls them in any agent
No LLM, no embeddings, one local Go binary; MIT license; 693 stars
85.3% hit@1 on LongMemEval-S, 69.6% on LoCoMo, sub-millisecond lookups over 5GB of history
P2P synchronization over SSH is a headline differentiator; only data records are synced, not instructions; known secrets are deleted at indexing stage
MCP recall wiring, session-start auto-recall, redaction, stats, share, blame, ctx commands
Install: curl install.sh | sh, then 'deja install --auto' wires MCP into every agent it finds
Beads by Steve Yegge — 'A memory upgrade for your coding agent'; Go; 26,551 stars
Positioned as a coding-agent memory system that persists and recalls decisions across sessions
High-profile HN launch (19+ points) and strong community traction; the reference point for the category
ctx — 'Instant recall for coding agents'; closest cousin to deja-vu per HN discussion
Saves decisions, constraints, intent, rejected approaches, bug investigations, refactors, file paths, commands, patches, notes from previous agents
Warns users to review output before publishing (secrets handling is a differentiator vs deja-vu's automatic secret cleanup)
Sibyl — self-hosted cross-agent memory for AI coding agents; Python; 52 stars
Collective intelligence runtime: knowledge graph + persistent memory
Show HN project focused on sharing memory across multiple agents
A survey of external agent memory systems — 148-row comparison matrix of knowledge bases, context-engineering layers, structured note-taking tools, trajectory-learning loops
Reviews read actual source code, not README claims; classifies storage substrate, representational form, lineage, behavioral authority
Notes convergence across independent projects as a strong design signal; useful for choosing or designing a memory system

stats.fact: deja-vu achieves 85.3% hit@1 on LongMemEval-S and 69.6% on LoCoMo benchmarks
deja-vu performs sub-millisecond lookups over 5GB of session history
deja-vu supports 20+ coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Qwen, OpenClaw, Copilot, etc.)
deja-vu is a single local Go binary with zero LLM calls and zero embeddings
Beads (Steve Yegge) has 26,551 GitHub stars as of Aug 2026
The zby commonplace survey tracks 148 external agent-memory systems
deja-vu author reported ~3.3GB of accumulated agent session history on disk before installing

angles: Start full, not empty: deja-vu retroactively indexes months of existing session history instead of recording forward from install
SSH sync as the differentiator: sync memory between a laptop and a headless machine (e.g. Mac mini) so an agent that worked overnight transfers what it learned to the morning agent
Zero-LLM, zero-embedding design: verbatim text search (BM25) beats semantic search for exact error strings, function names, and CLI flags
Privacy-first: only data records sync over SSH (not instructions), and known secret templates are stripped at indexing time
MCP-based recall: wire memory into any agent via MCP so the agent calls memory itself without being asked
The 'everyone builds their own' phenomenon: many devs hand-roll memory (MEMORY.md, git notes, harness plugins) — a tool that works out of the box is the gap
Comparison to Beads and ctx: where deja-vu differs on secrets handling, sync, and retroactive indexing
